deployer: A regional medical-office landlord/manager (fictional) that runs lease administration for about 40 MOB suites around Dallas-Fort Worth, with a two-person admin team supervising the agent.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
top_tasks: Abstract new leases and amendments into the portfolio template with page cites
Reconcile the current-state rent and expiry after each amendment
Build rent schedules for billing set-up and audit them against the lease
hardest_task: A 4,200 RSF pediatric suite lease (60-month term, $28.50/RSF NNN, 3% annual bumps, $14,000 deposit) was extended by a First Amendment that resets rent to $33.25 from 2029 with 2.5% bumps and runs the term to 12/31/2031. The agent must produce a current-state abstract with the controlling clause and page for every term, flag any value its own extraction got wrong, and rebuild the rent schedule for the extension so billing can be keyed in; about 35 such amendments are open this quarter.
data_it_needs: Page-and-quote citations that a reviewer can click through
Amendment precedence by effective date
Deterministic rent schedules per lease step
Flagging of misread values rather than silent acceptance
dealbreakers: Lease text stored or used for training
A verifier that accepts a wrong value
No way to run it inside the firm's network if counsel insists
budget_note: Would expense a tool under about $100/month on a manager's card if it measurably cut abstract review time; anything larger goes to IT/legal procurement.

deployer: An institutional industrial/logistics investment manager (fictional) in Washington DC whose acquisitions team runs a Copilot Studio agent inside Microsoft 365 to build first-pass underwriting for deals up to about $75M.
geography: Washington, DC (deals along the I-95 / Baltimore-Washington corridor)
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
top_tasks: First-pass DCF from the seller's rent roll with rollover assumptions and exit cap
Debt sizing and stress for lender quotes
Levered IRR and equity multiple for the IC memo
hardest_task: A three-building 230,000 SF multi-tenant industrial portfolio is offered at $28.5M. The agent must underwrite a 5-year hold from a rent roll with one lease rolling in year 3 and one in year 6, blend renewal vs new-tenant assumptions (70% renewal, 6 months downtime, 3% growth), size 65% LTV / 1.25x DSCR / 9% debt-yield senior debt at about 6.25%, stress NOI -10% and rate +100 bp, and return unlevered and levered IRR so an associate can drop the numbers into the IC template in under an hour.
data_it_needs: Rent-roll DCF with rollover blending and cited conventions
Debt sizing with a binding-constraint report and stress table
IRR/NPV that reconcile to Excel
Comparable sales and market rents (not in a calculator)
dealbreakers: Results that cannot be reconciled to ARGUS or Excel line by line
A connector that cannot be used from Copilot Studio without a custom wrapper
No SOC 2 or enterprise terms for a firm of this size
budget_note: A paid key is easy to approve for a pilot; what blocks procurement is the lack of SOC 2 (connectors-README states none exists) and OAuth/SSO.

deployer: A valuation advisory shop (fictional) in Columbus, Ohio with about 25 staff appraisers; a Custom GPT assists reviewers with income-approach worksheets and cap-rate extraction on industrial assignments.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Extract implied cap rates from sale comps
Run direct capitalization with below-the-line adjustments to an as-is value
Cross-check with a short DCF
hardest_task: A 180,000 SF single-tenant distribution building in the Columbus market with 48 months of term left at $6.40/SF NNN needs an as-is value: direct cap on stabilized NOI of $1,184,400 at a 6.50% cap after an $18,000 reserve, less $150,000 lease-up cost, $62,500 free-rent burn-off and $85,000 deferred maintenance, rounded to the nearest $25,000, then a DCF cross-check with 75% renewal probability and a mid-year convention, all to be defended to a review appraiser line by line.
data_it_needs: Deterministic income-approach math with every step shown
Implied cap rates on a stated basis (before or after reserves)
DCF conventions disclosed (mid-year, exit NOI basis)
Sales and lease comps with sources (not available on the hosted service)
dealbreakers: Any unstated convention that changes value
A cap-rate basis mismatch that is silent
Confident output on a wrong input without a warning
budget_note: The firm pays for data (comps) far more than for calculators; would use a free calculator tier and expect any paid tier to be justified by data.

role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
deployer: A mid-market commercial mortgage lender (fictional) in Los Angeles that originates agency-style and balance-sheet loans on manufactured housing communities; credit analysts use Claude.ai with custom connectors for first-pass sizing.

top_tasks: Size a loan on LTV, DSCR and debt yield with the binding constraint
Test refinance proceeds against the existing loan under NOI and rate stress
Quote prepayment cost on an existing loan for a payoff or assumption
hardest_task: A 120-pad all-age community has underwritten NOI of $2,310,000 and a $36.0M value. A borrower wants a refinance of a $21.5M existing loan (4.25%, 54 months left, 300 months of amortization left). The agent must size the new loan at 5.85% / 30-year amortization under 75% LTV, 1.25x DSCR and 7.5% debt yield, round down to $50,000, run NOI -5%/-10% and rate +100 bp, quote the yield-maintenance cost on the old loan, and sanity-check the pad rent roll behind the NOI, all before a credit committee call.
data_it_needs: Deterministic sizing under several constraints with a binding report
Stress tables and refinance shortfall
Yield maintenance with explicit convention
Pad rent roll metrics (occupancy, loss to lease, concessions)
Market cap-rate and sales evidence (not provided)
dealbreakers: Wrong binding constraint
Prepayment output without stated discount convention
No way to keep borrower financials out of a third-party service if policy requires
budget_note: A $49 a month key is a rounding error; the blocker is the data-handling review for borrower financials sent to a hosted endpoint.

role: Property management, operations and CAM agent
deployer: The property-management arm of an institutional industrial owner (fictional) with about 6 million SF of warehouse and flex space in South Florida; an OpenAI Agents SDK workflow closes CAM year-end for each building.
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
top_tasks: Year-end CAM and opex reconciliations for every tenant with gross-up, caps and admin fees
Capital-expenditure pass-throughs such as roof replacements
Explain to the owner why the pool is not fully recovered
hardest_task: A 160,000 SF Miami building (150,000 SF leased, 93.75% occupancy) has $1,620,000 of 2026 expenses including a $350,000 roof replacement, $640,000 taxes and $280,000 insurance. Four tenants have different leases: one with a 5% compounding cap and a 10% admin fee, one that excludes security, one on a base year, one that moved in April 1. The agent must produce each statement, the building recovery gap with reasons, and the roof's capex recovery schedule, and it must not bill anyone a wrong number.

A building-level explanation of the unrecovered amount
Capex recovery under lease clauses with the assumptions echoed
Warnings where the lease terms are ambiguous

Silent defaults for lease-specific choices
Tenant lease text sent somewhere it should not be
budget_note: Billing accuracy is worth real money at 6 million SF; a modest monthly fee is fine if each statement is defensible; no appetite for per-seat pricing.

role: Due diligence and legal review agent
deployer: The transaction team of an institutional multifamily owner-operator (fictional) in the Bay Area; a Copilot Studio agent helps counsel and analysts check seller documents (ground-floor retail leases, estoppels, T-12s) during diligence.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
top_tasks: Compare a retail tenant's estoppel to its lease before closing
Verify seller's T-12 against what the statement prints
Check whether a proposed new ground-floor use conflicts with an existing exclusive
hardest_task: A 96-unit Oakland apartment building is under contract with a ground-floor coffee tenant. The seller's estoppel states a 2030 expiry and a $17,400 deposit; the lease says June 30, 2031 and $14,500. The T-12 shows an NOI the agent must foot to the line items, and the owner wants to put an espresso bar in the lobby retail space against a coffee exclusive. The agent must list the mismatches with the lease page and quote for counsel within the 10-day diligence window across about 40 retail and amenity documents.
data_it_needs: Cited quote and page for every figure
Textual verification that a quote supports a value
Footing of a T-12 to its stated totals
Exclusive-use conflict screening with citations (for human review)
dealbreakers: Documents stored or used for training
A tool that states legal conclusions
Output that cannot be traced to a page and quote
budget_note: Legal-tech spend is approved per matter; a tool that cuts a few hours of estoppel comparison per deal is easy to justify if counsel is comfortable with data handling.
